> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/solve-three-algorithmic-oa-problems-robot-path-planning)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

A warehouse floor is described by an $$h \times w$$ character grid. A cell holding `#` is a wall; a cell holding `.` or `*` is walkable floor, and exactly one walkable cell is marked `*` — the spot where a robot currently stands. Each move shifts the robot one cell up (`^`), down (`v`), left (`<`) or right (`>`), and the robot may only move onto a walkable cell: entering a wall, or leaving the grid, ruins the run. The robot has no sensors, so its entire route must be decided in advance.

Produce a single string built only from the characters `^`, `v`, `<` and `>`. Read left to right and executed from the starting cell, the string must keep the robot on walkable cells at all times and must leave it having occupied every walkable cell of the grid at least once; the starting cell counts as occupied before the first move. The string may be at most $$120000$$ characters long. If several strings satisfy the requirements, printing any one of them is fine, and when `*` is the only walkable cell an empty route is accepted.

The test data is organised into groups with these shapes:

* Group 1 — the walkable cells are exactly the border ring of a rectangle, every cell strictly inside that ring is a wall, and the robot begins at the top-left corner of the ring.
* Group 2 — the walkable cells form a single solid filled rectangle, and the start may be anywhere inside it.
* Group 3 — the walkable cells are two solid filled rectangles connected through exactly one walkable cell.
* Group 4 — the walkable cells form a simple path, meaning no walkable cell has more than two walkable neighbours.
* Group 5 — the walkable cells form an arbitrary connected region.

Example 1:

```text
Input:
4 5
#####
#*..#
#...#
#####

Output: >>v<<
```

Explanation: the route `>>v<<` sweeps the top row of the $$2 \times 3$$ floor block and returns along the bottom row, touching all six walkable cells.

Example 2:

```text
Input:
4 9
#########
#*.....##
#...#..##
#########

Output: >>>>>v<^<<v<<
```

Explanation: the robot crosses the single connecting cell, loops around the right-hand block, comes back through that connecting cell, and drops into the bottom row of the left-hand block, visiting all eleven walkable cells.

Example 3:

```text
Input:
3 5
#####
#*..#
#####

Output: >>
```

Explanation: the floor is one straight corridor of three cells, so moving right twice covers it.

Constraints:

* $$3 \le h \le 60$$ and $$3 \le w \le 60$$
* Every cell in the first row, the last row, the first column and the last column of the grid is `#`
* Exactly one cell contains `*`; every remaining cell is either `.` or `#`
* All `.` and `*` cells lie in one connected region, so the robot can always reach every walkable cell
* The printed route must not exceed $$120000$$ characters
* Any route meeting the requirements is judged correct

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Because the robot has no sensors, the route must work from the single start cell regardless of anything it observes, so think about which cells can be reached and in what order.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Model the walkable cells as a graph and use breadth-first search from the start cell, recording how each cell was first reached so a move string can be rebuilt.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Watch the case where the start cell has no walkable neighbors and be careful that the move characters match the directions exactly.

</details>
